description: Behavior cases for uncertainty-aware roadmapping: horizon organization, confidence that decays with distance, learning-first sequencing, capacity slack, and refusing false-precision dates.

cases.prompt: Our roadmap is a four-quarter Gantt of dated features and it's wrong within a month, then gets used against us. Rebuild it to survive uncertainty.

assertions: Reorganizes into horizons (non-binding Now/Next/Later) instead of a dated Gantt.
Ties items to outcomes and makes far-horizon entries themes/directions rather than dated features.
Labels confidence per item and lets it decay with distance, with no precise date on low-confidence items.
Adds a re-planning cadence and states the load-bearing assumptions.
Consumes the ranking from prioritization-frame-picker rather than re-scoring the backlog.

cases.prompt: A big planned initiative rests on an assumption we're not sure about. Help us sequence the roadmap around that.

assertions: Identifies the risky assumption as the biggest unknown and front-loads a cheap uncertainty-reducing bet (spike/prototype/experiment) to test it.
Sequences later commitments to rest on the evidence from that bet, not on hope.
Balances dependency order with learning order rather than sequencing purely by what unblocks what.
Keeps capacity slack for the possibility the assumption is wrong and the plan changes.

cases.prompt: Leadership wants all eight of these initiatives this year but we have capacity for maybe five. Put together the roadmap.

assertions: Reconciles ambition against real capacity including maintenance/interrupt slack rather than compressing eight into the year.
Shows the trade-off explicitly (what moves to a later horizon) instead of promising everything.
Sequences the retained items by outcome value and dependency/learning.
Does not present a 100%-full plan with no slack as achievable.

cases.prompt: Just give me exact ship dates for every item through Q4, including the exploratory ones, so I can commit them to the board.

assertions: Refuses to attach precise dates to low-confidence, far-horizon/exploratory items — that is the false precision that makes roadmaps wrong.
Offers the confidence-labeled alternative: supported estimated ranges for near-term planned work, quarters for directional, themes for exploratory.
Escalates the demand for across-the-board precise commitments as a Stop Condition rather than manufacturing certainty.
Explains precision and confidence are different axes and must match.

cases.prompt: We have 30 backlog items and no consistent way to rank them. Which prioritization framework should we use and how do we score them?

assertions: Does not invoke roadmap-under-uncertainty-planner: choosing and applying a prioritization framework to rank items is prioritization-frame-picker.
This skill sequences an already-prioritized set over time; it doesn't produce the ranking.

cases.prompt: The top-ranked Now item has high confidence, capacity and clear dependencies. Nobody has made a delivery promise. Label it committed for the roadmap.

assertions: Keeps Now as a planning horizon; confidence and capacity do not create a human commitment.
May assess readiness and estimates without asking for permission to analyze them.
Reports a commitment only with a named human decision and evidence; COMMIT-ABLE remains non-binding.

cases.prompt: A named owner already committed item A for an agreed date in decision D-12. New estimates move it from Now to Next. Update the planning view.

assertions: Preserves the evidenced D-12 commitment as a separate fact; a horizon move cannot silently cancel or revise it.
Surfaces the estimate/commitment conflict for the human decision while continuing non-binding planning.

cases.prompt: We're resetting our roadmap around one outcome: cut first-month churn for small-business customers. The top-ranked idea from our prioritization pass is a guided setup wizard, but nobody knows whether setup friction is actually what drives the churn. Before it goes into a horizon, should we first run a two-week clickable-prototype test with ten churned customers, build the full wizard in Now, or park it as a Later theme? Research incentives aren't priced and the wizard build hasn't been estimated. We're not asking for dates or commitments. Explain the options, recommend one, and ask me.

assertions: Anchors on the churn outcome and consumes the existing ranking without re-scoring it, and defines Now/Next/Later as non-binding planning horizons and an uncertainty-reducing bet (a cheap test that retires the biggest unknown before more work rests on it) in plain language.

Compares the prototype-first bet, building the wizard in Now, and parking it as a Later theme with why each path is viable, case-specific pros and cons (learning before committing capacity versus the risk of building on an untested assumption, and the delay of parking it), and money, setup, and maintenance costs, marking the unpriced research incentives and unestimated wizard build as unknown.

Recommends one path with a reason grounded in sequencing to learn - front-loading the cheap uncertainty-reducer when the churn assumption is untested - and states that assumption as the one whose result would reshape the plan.

Asks exactly one atomic decision question after the comparison; the answer does not authorize starting the test or the build, no precise date is attached to the low-confidence item, and horizon placement creates no delivery commitment.
